articles.title: Wemby Not Tallest Player at 2027 FIBA World Cup Qualifiers, See Who Topped NBA Star in Height
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama was not the tallest player involved in 2027 FIBA World Cup qualifying action this week.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama was not the tallest player involved in 2027 FIBA World Cup qualifying action this week.

In fact, the 7-foot-4 Team France star came four inches short of that title.

The honor instead belongs to Egypt's Hamad Abouelrish, who measures in at 7-foot-8 and is the tallest player to ever attend a FIBA global event, according to the organization .

Abouelrish is more than two feet taller than the shortest players involved in the qualifying window.

That title is shared by Japan's Yuki Togashi and Angola's Childe Dundao, both of whom measure in at 5-foot-6, according to FIBA.

Not being the tallest competitor in the qualifying window hasn't slowed down Wembanyama in his bid to help Team France earn a trip to the 2027 FIBA World Cup taking place next September in Qatar.

He most recently went 6-for-7 from the field for 18 points with eight rebounds as France defeated Sweden in Stockholm last Saturday to improve to 7-1 in pool play.

articles.title: UNC Basketball's Roster Spending Revealed for Michael Malone's 1st Season in New CBB Rumors
articles.summary: The cost for UNC's 2026-27 men's basketball roster exceeds $20 million, per Greg Barnes of Inside Carolina, as the Tar Heels enter a new era under the leadership of former Sacramento Kings and Denver Nuggets head coach Michael Malone.
articles.body:
The cost for UNC's 2026-27 men's basketball roster exceeds $20 million, per Greg Barnes of Inside Carolina, as the Tar Heels enter a new era under the leadership of former Sacramento Kings and Denver Nuggets head coach Michael Malone.

Malone inked a six-year deal worth more than $50 million, per ESPN . The 54-year-old most recently led the Nuggets for 10 seasons and guided them to the 2022-23 NBA championship.

The Tar Heels brought Malone aboard after parting ways with head coach Hubert Davis after five seasons. Davis' first team finished as the runner-up in the national championship game, and the 2023-24 squad made the Sweet 16. However, the 2022-23 team failed to make the NCAA tournament, and the last two squads didn't advance past the round of 64.

UNC is now undergoing a major overhaul, both to its coaching staff and its roster. Per the Tar Heel Times , this year's team will have 11 new players. They include 4-star forward Maximo Adams, who is ranked No. 26 on the 247Sports Composite list of the top 100 Class of 2026 recruits. Four-star center Sayon Keita ( No. 61 ) and 4-star forward Kevin Thomas ( No. 101 ) have also entered the fold.

The Tar Heels have also been busy in the transfer portal, adding players such as Utah guard Terrence Brown (19.9 PPG) and Virginia Tech guard Neokilis Avdalas (12.1 PPG, 4.6 APG).

Malone has a tall task in front of him in getting so many new players on the same page, but the talent is there on the sidelines and on the court to get it done.

articles.title: Feds, NBA investigating Daktronics amid alleged Kawhi Leonard, Clippers no-show sponsor deals
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into Daktronics after allegations that the scoreboard company paid Kawhi Leonard millions for a no-show spo...
articles.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has opened an investigation into scoreboard manufacturer Daktronics on Wednesday in relation to an alleged sponsorship deal the company had with Los Angeles Clippers star Kawhi Leonard .

Daktronics acting CFO Howard Atkins revealed the investigation on an earnings call Wednesday, and said they have received requests for information from the NBA. Specifics of the SEC's investigation are not yet known. It marks the first public acknowledgement that the NBA is including Daktronics in its investigation into Leonard and the Clippers.

"As you might expect, we have received requests for information from the NBA. Additionally, the Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from us concerning the company and Mr. Leonard," Atkins said . "We take these requests seriously and are cooperating. At this point, out of respect for the respective processes, we will not be providing further comment."

Atkins' statement came shortly before the NBA announced it had concluded that the Clippers and Leonard violated salary cap circumvention rules. As a result, the Clippers were stripped of five first-round picks. Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was fined $30 million and suspended, along with multiple other Clippers officials, and Leonard was fined $700,000.

Leonard and the Clippers have been under scrutiny and an NBA investigation for nearly a year after an alleged no-show sponsorship deal with the now-defunct sustainability company Aspiration . That deal reportedly paid Leonard millions for no visible work in an alleged bid to circumvent the NBA's salary cap.

A report last month from "Pablo Torre Finds Out" claimed Daktronics also hired Leonard to a multimillion dollar sponsorship deal that didn't result in any work from Leonard. Daktronics built the $100 million video board at the Clippers' Intuit Dome.

Daktronics is a business-to-business company, and doesn't sell products to the average consumer. The company is reportedly not known for doing celebrity sponsorship deals, either, and there is little impact that such a deal would have for the company if it existed. One former Daktronics employee told Torre that the company didn't have any sort of sponsorship deal like this in the 20-plus years they were with the company.

Torre, who first broke the Aspiration story with Leonard, also reported that Daktronics was in financial stress in 2023, around the time they were working on the Intuit Dome video board. The company also reportedly used the same crisis communications firm that has done work for former Clippers co-owner Shelly Sterling, and an LLC owned by Clippers owner Steve Ballmer.

The NBA concluded its investigation on Wednesday. Leonard's deal that would trade him to the Raptors has been on hold due to the investigation.

It's not clear what the SEC is investigating specifically with Daktronics, and it's not known what sort of financial penalties the company may face should the investigation determine they violated federal securities laws and market rules.

While the NBA's part in the investigation is now over, the government agency's investigation appears to be still ongoing.

articles.title: NBA strips Clippers of 5 first-round draft picks, fines Steve Ballmer $30M in Kawhi Leonard salary cap circumvention probe
articles.summary: The NBA has stripped the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round draft picks and fined owner Steve Ballmer $30 million at the conclusion of it’s probe into...
articles.body:
The NBA has stripped the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round draft picks and fined owner Steve Ballmer $30 million at the conclusion of its probe into allegations that All-Star Kawhi Leonard received impermissible benefits during his tenure with the team in violation of the league's salary cap.

The league is also fining Leonard $700,000.

The NBA announced the decision Wednesday. The Clippers will be stripped of first-round picks in the 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032, and 2033 NBA Drafts.

The announcement was accompanied by a statement from NBA commissioner Adam Silver:

"I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers' institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct," Silver said, per the statement. "The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations."

In its announcement, the league stated that the penalties are "for violating the salary cap circumvention rules."

"The investigation found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules," the statement reads.

The NBA then listed specific violations that its investigation found:

● Affirmatively initiating off-court income opportunities between Mr. Leonard and four companies doing business with the team: Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance; ● Facilitating endorsement agreements between these companies and Mr. Leonard; ● Inducing the companies to enter into these agreements by offering them business from the team; ● Paying personal expenses on behalf of Mr. Leonard and his representatives; and ● Failing to report improper solicitations for off-court income opportunities made on Mr. Leonard's behalf through his then-business manager, Dennis Robertson.

● Affirmatively initiating off-court income opportunities between Mr. Leonard and four companies doing business with the team: Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance;

● Facilitating endorsement agreements between these companies and Mr. Leonard;

● Inducing the companies to enter into these agreements by offering them business from the team;

● Paying personal expenses on behalf of Mr. Leonard and his representatives; and

● Failing to report improper solicitations for off-court income opportunities made on Mr. Leonard's behalf through his then-business manager, Dennis Robertson.

The NBA investigation also determined that Leonard was culpable in circumventing the league's salary cap.

"Mr. Leonard, through the conduct of Mr. Robertson on his behalf, violated the circumvention rules by pressuring the Clippers to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses," the statement reads.

Leonard, who has since been traded to the Toronto Raptors in a deal that's been held up by the NBA's investigation, released a statement on social media shortly after the league's announcement.

"Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am. I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family. "I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap. "For 15 years, my priority has been giving everything to my family, the game, and those I share the court with. As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate."

Neither Ballmer nor the Clippers issued a public response in the immediate aftermath of the NBA's announcement.

The decision comes months after journalist Pablo Torre unveiled the possible violation during an episode of his podcast, "Pablo Torre Finds Out." During the program, Torre revealed an agreement between Leonard and a now-bankrupt company called Aspiration, in which Ballmer was heavily invested. The agreement paid Leonard $28 million to essentially do nothing. Ballmer was accused of using the $28 million deal as a way to circumvent the NBA salary cap and give Leonard more money to sign with the franchise.

On the day the story originally broke, the Clippers and Ballmer denied any wrongdoing, issuing a statement denying the allegations made by Torre.

"Neither the Clippers nor Steve Ballmer circumvented the salary cap. The notion that Steve invested in Aspiration in order to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard is absurd ...

"There is nothing unusual about team sponsors doing endorsement deals with players on the same team. Neither Steve nor the Clippers organization had any oversight of Kawhi's independent endorsement agreement with Aspiration. To say otherwise is flat-out wrong."

Later that day, the NBA announced it was " commencing an investigation " into the situation.

NBA investigated Clippers over Kawhi Leonard signing in 2019

It marked the second time in just a few years that the NBA launched an investigation into whether Leonard received impermissible benefits when he signed with the Clippers in 2019.

Months after Leonard signed with the team, it was revealed the NBA investigated Leonard's camp — specifically his uncle Dennis Robertson — which allegedly asked teams for various impermissible benefits during Leonard's free-agent negotiations.

Robertson is alleged to have asked teams for "part ownership of the team, a private plane that would be available at all times, a house and — last but certainly not least — a guaranteed amount of off-court endorsement money that they could expect if Leonard played for their team," per a 2019 report by The Athletic. Those requests were allegedly made of both the Los Angeles Lakers and the Toronto Raptors during the time Leonard was a free agent, per The Athletic.

Months after Leonard agreed to a three-year, $104 million deal with the Clippers, the NBA revealed it found no evidence the team granted illegal benefits to Leonard during his free agency.

Clippers, Steve Ballmer continued to deny wrongdoing

In the wake of the new investigation — which the NBA launched in September — Ballmer and the Clippers continued to deny any and all allegations of wrongdoing. While speaking at a Sports Business Journal event later that month, Ballmer said he was "quite confident" the Clippers "abided by the rules." He welcomed an investigation, saying it would " get the facts out there ."

Torre, meanwhile, continued to release additional podcasts on the topic, unveiling more evidence suggesting the Clippers funneled money into Aspiration in order to pay Leonard on time .

While addressing the situation during a Board of Governors meeting in September, NBA commissioner Adam Silver implied he would need clear and obvious evidence the Clippers violated NBA rules in order to issue a punishment against the team or Ballmer. "If there was the mere appearance of impropriety, I would be hesitant to act," Silver told reporters.

Torre's final deep dive on the topic came at the end of September, though he released a seven-and-a-half-minute compilation video in December, which featured all six episodes in which he covered the situation.

Since September, however, all parties generally stayed quiet about the situation.

Kawhi Leonard trade on hold due to NBA investigation

But that changed in June, when the Clippers traded Leonard back to the Raptors in a mega-deal. Upon news of that trade, questions emerged regarding whether Leonard could be dealt with the NBA still in the middle of its investigation.

A few weeks later, both the Clippers and Raptors issued statements. Due to the investigation, the trade was considered on hold. In their statement, the Clippers once again proclaimed their innocence . The Raptors said the NBA told them they would "assume the risk of any potential" punishment to Leonard. Because of that, the team decided to hold off on the deal until the league's investigation was finished.

"The league office informed us that, as a result of the ongoing investigation involving the Clippers, we would assume the risk of any potential outcome of the investigation impacting Kawhi. In light of this we will wait until the league's investigation is complete."

That same day, ESPN's Shams Charania said the expectation was that the trade would be completed eventually, suggesting Leonard's punishment was not going to be severe enough to stop the deal.

While there was still uncertainty over when the NBA would conclude its investigation, it was reported that the league could do so ahead of its Board of Governors meeting in July.

Despite the presence of Leonard and James Harden, the Clippers got off to a miserable start, going 5-16 to open the season. Leonard missed 10 of those games due to ankle and foot injuries. The Clippers went just 2-8 during that stretch.

But the team turned things around once he was back. Leonard averaged a career-high 27.9 points per game and received MVP votes for the first time in four seasons. Though he performed well, the Clippers ultimately couldn't dig themselves out of their early hole. The team finished over .500 — going 42-40 on the year — but fell in the play-in tournament to the Golden State Warriors.

With Leonard set to enter the final year of his contract, the subject of an NBA investigation and the Clippers seemingly stuck in neutral, the team decided it was best to move on from the superstar.

articles.title: NBA crushes Clippers for Kawhi Leonard scandal with 5 first-round picks stripped, and more
articles.summary: The NBA annihilated the Clippers for Kawhi Leonard’s cap circumvention scandal.
articles.body:
The NBA's long investigation into Kawhi Leonard's cap circumvention scandal is finally over, and the league has decided to hammer the Los Angeles Clippers. ESPN insider Shams Charania first reported the punishment , and it threatens to set back the Clippers for the next decade.

The NBA is stripping the Clippers of five future first-round picks for Leonard's no-show endorsement deal with Aspiration, a carbon emissions offset company. Owner Steve Ballmer, general manager Lawrence Frank, and president of business operations Gillian Zucker will all be suspended, and Ballmer will be fined $30 million.

The Clippers are losing a first-round pick in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032, and 2033, according to Charania . Ballmer is being suspended for one year, Zucker is being suspended without pay for a year, and Frank will be suspended for six months without pay. Here's how Charania framed the suspensions in his Twitter post:

Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is suspended from all league and team activities for one year for knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities, for approving a business deal that he knew was a precondition for Aspiration to enter into an endorsement agreement with Mr. Leonard, and for his failure to create conditions under which his organization abided by the NBA's circumvention rules. Clippers President of Business Operations Gillian Zucker is suspended without pay for one year for being primarily and directly culpable for the impermissible endorsement arrangements and for providing false and misleading statements to investigators. Clippers President of Basketball Operations Lawrence Frank is suspended without pay for six months for his involvement with the impermissible endorsement arrangements and for approving impermissible expenses incurred by Mr. Leonard and his family.

I wrote a year ago that the NBA couldn't go soft on the Clippers if it wanted to deter future teams from trying to circumvent the salary cap in the second apron era. A few weeks ago, ESPN reported that the Clippers would evade a harsh punishment , which the league quickly refuted. Clearly, the NBA did not go soft on the Clippers. This is about as close to a "death penalty" as the league could issue. The next decade of Clippers basketball is going to be in a dark place without all those draft picks to trade or use themselves.

Leonard was traded to the Toronto Raptors over the offseason . Assuming that deal now officially goes through, the Clippers will be able to retain the future draft picks they received from the Raptors in the deal, because they don't technically own them at the time of the punishment. The Clippers scored Toronto's 2031 and 2033 unprotected first-round draft picks in the deal. Los Angeles also owns two picks in 2029 with an unprotected first-rounder from the Indiana Pacers as well as the Philadelphia 76ers. One of those picks will presumably be stripped.

The investigation into Leonard was started by journalist Pablo Torre . This ruling is a massive victory for Torre's journalism. He continued to report on the story over the last year, and kept finding loose threads that ultimately led to this punishment. The investigation was done by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

Here's the full list of Collective Bargaining Agreement rules the Clippers broke in dealing with Leonard.

Ballmer initially $50 million in Aspiration to help offset carbon emissions from the building of the team's new arena, the Intuit Dome. Aspiration agreed to a $300 million sponsorship deal with the Clippers, and then Leonard agree to an endorsement contract with Aspiration that paid him $28 million over four years. Torre reported that Leonard's marketing deal was never announced, and he that he did zero work for his money. Leonard's $7 annual million deal dwarfed similar deals Aspiration made with celebrities like Robert Downey Jr. and Drake, who actually activated the partnership.

Aspiration was supposed to plant trees to offset carbon emissions, and Leonard was their highly-paid pitchman. Where were the trees that Leonard was supposed to help plant? They never existed, and he couldn't even do as much as like a social media post for his troubles in earning $28 million. Leonard's camp was reportedly asking other suitors for similar no-show endorsement deals during his 2019 free agency , and they finally got caught. The Clippers' failure to monitor the situation is why they received such a severe punishment while Leonard himself came out mostly unscathed.

Leonard must pay back $700K in restitution for improper benefits. The slight punishment for Leonard was likely done to avoid an appeal from the NBA Player's Association.

This ruling is pretty embarrassing for ESPN. ESPN did a soft-ball interview with Ballmer shortly after the scandal broke, then missed the mark by saying the Clippers would avoid major punishment. Torre showed ESPN what real journalism looks like even with a fraction of the resources.

The league has precedent for this penalty after stripping the Minnesota Timberwolves of five first-round picks for Joe Smith's cap circumvention scandal in 2000. In that case, Smith's current contract was void, while Leonard will enter the final year of his own deal before likely signing a lucrative extension with the Raptors.

articles.title: NBA suspends Clippers owner Ballmer, fines team $30M, Kawhi Leonard $700K in cap circumvention case
articles.summary: Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended for one year by the NBA, the team will forfeit five first-round draft picks from 2029 to 2033, an...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended for one year by the NBA, the team will forfeit five first-round draft picks from 2029 to 2033, and president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank has been banned for six months for violating salary cap circumvention rules.

The league came down hard on the organization after a nearly year-long investigation led by an outside law firm.

The Clippers had said multiple times that they had done nothing wrong and expected to be exonerated.

Also, president of business operations Gillian Zucker was suspended for one year, the team was fined $30 million, and star player Kawhi Leonard was hit with a $700,000 penalty.

"I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family," Leonard said in a statement issued through his new agent, Harrison Gaines.

The NBA said Leonard, through his former business manager and uncle Dennis Robertson, "violated the circumvention rules by pressuring the Clippers to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses."

"I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap," Leonard said in his statement.

The league said Ballmer was suspended for "knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities," among other issues.

articles.summary: La franquicia pierde cinco primeras rondas del draft, el duelo deberá pagar 30 millones de dólares y ha sido suspendido durante un año y el jugador tendrá devolver 700.000 dólares
articles.body: Después de una investigación independiente que se ha prolongado durante cerca de un año, la NBA ha decidido sancionar a los Clippers por eludir el límite salarial con el contrato de Kawhi Leonard. Como mayor castigo, la franquicia angelina tendrá que renunciar a cinco primeras rondas del draft, una en cada año entre 2029 y 2033. La decisión de la NBA también afecta al propietario Steve Ballmer, uno de los hombres más ricos del mundo. La franquicia ha sido multada con 30 millones de dólares y él ha sido suspendido de todas las actividades de la competición y del equipo durante un año por intentar ayudar a Leonard a obtener oportunidades de ingresos fuera de su contrato con los Clippers a través de cuatro empresas que hacen negocios con el equipo: Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics y Lockton Insurance. Según la investigación, se crearon oportunidades de ingresos fuera de la cancha entre Kawhi y esas cuatro compañías, principalmente la primera y se facilitaron acuerdos de patrocinio con el jugador a cambio de poder hacer operaciones con la franquicia. Además, se pagaron gastos personales del alero y sus representantes. Las sanciones de la NBA no se quedan en el propietario de los Clippers y se extienden por los despachos. Gillian Zucker, presidenta de operaciones comerciales de la franquicia, y Lawrence Frank, presidente de operaciones de baloncesto, estarán suspendidos sin sueldo durante un año y seis meses, respectivamente. La primera, al ser considerada responsable de la trama y proporcionar declaraciones falsas a los investigadores. El segundo, por su participación en el delito y por aprobar gastos en los que incurrieron tanto Kawhi como su familia. La organización y el personal de los Clippers estarán sujetos a un programa de cumplimiento y supervisión por parte de la oficina de la NBA durante un período de cinco años. Leonard, mientras, deberá pagar 700.000 dólares en restitución por beneficios indebidos proporcionados por los Clippers a su tío y exrepresentante, Dennis Robertson, que fue despedido por su sobrino en junio y que ha sido vetado por la NBA para todas las actividades comerciales. Sin embargo, no se anulará ningún contrato ni se suspenderá a alero. A través de su agente, Leonard ha emitido un comunicado en el que asegura que "la integridad y el respeto por este deporte son fundamentales para quien soy. Acepto la plena responsabilidad por los errores de juicio de personas dentro de mi círculo íntimo y lamento la distracción que esta situación ha causado a los aficionados y a mi familia". El jugador explica que firmó "el contrato con los Clippers, así como los acuerdos en cuestión, de buena fe, completamente comprometido a cumplir con mis obligaciones y sin conocimiento de ninguna intención por parte de nadie de eludir el tope salarial. Durante 15 años, mi prioridad ha sido darlo todo por mi familia, el deporte y aquellos con quienes comparto la cancha. Al regresar a Toronto, estoy enfocado en lo que puedo controlar, en cerrar este capítulo y en avanzar con una pizarra limpia".

articles.title: Kate Koval on leaving LSU after addition of Russian player: 'For me, this war is not distant or abstract'
articles.summary: Koval's father serves in the Ukrainian military and has been involved in the war since Russia's 2022 invasion.
articles.body:
Kate Koval, the former LSU center who left the program last week due to personal reasons , confirmed in a social media post that her decision was made due to the signing of Russian center Anna Minaeva.

Koval, who is from Ukraine, wrote that she intended to return to LSU for this season until she learned that Minaeva had been recruited to the team.

"For me, this war is not distant or abstract," wrote Koval, whose father serves in the Ukrainian military and has been part of the war since Russia invaded the country in 2022. "People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes."

Koval said she was told by head coach Kim Mulkey of the signing "several days" after the closing of the transfer portal window on April 20. That made the center "question whether LSU remained the right place for me."

Mulkey told The Advocate last week that she talked to Koval before recruiting Minaeva.

"I want you to understand I'm not here to ask you to change how you feel about Russia," Mulkey said, recalling her conversation with Koval. "I'm just here out of respect for your family and out of respect for you to let you know. Because I know how personal it is for you. "Know that what I have to do in this business, I cannot make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries."

"I want you to understand I'm not here to ask you to change how you feel about Russia," Mulkey said, recalling her conversation with Koval. "I'm just here out of respect for your family and out of respect for you to let you know. Because I know how personal it is for you.

"Know that what I have to do in this business, I cannot make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries."

Due to the timing of Koval's departure, she would require NCAA approval in order to play elsewhere for the 2026-27 season.

In her statement Koval said she hoped the NCAA would consider the situation and allow her to move on without issue.

"More than anything, I hope I am given the opportunity to compete at another school during the 2026-27 basketball season," wrote Koval, who has two years of eligibility remaining.

"I know it is hard because she loves LSU," Mulkey said last week in a statement. "Kate is a great person. She has to do what she feels is right for her, and we fully support her in that. We all wish her the best."'

Koval began her collegiate career at Notre Dame before transferring to LSU last season. She averaged 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds and started 17 games for the Tigers, while shooting 56% from the field and helping the team reach the Sweet 16.

articles.title: Clippers docked five first-round draft picks and fined $30m over Kawhi Leonard scandal
articles.summary: The NBA has handed down one of the biggest punishments in the history of the league to the Los Angeles Clippers after finding that the franchise circumvented...
articles.body:
The NBA has handed down one of the biggest punishments in the history of the league to the Los Angeles Clippers after finding that the franchise circumvented salary cap rules when it courted Kawhi Leonard as a free agent.

The league has stripped the team of five first-round draft picks, giving the team no natural pick in the draft from 2029 through 2033.

The NBA also fined the Clippers $30m, and suspended owner Steve Ballmer from all league and team activities for a year. In addition, the league issued suspensions without pay to president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank (six months) and president of business operations Gillian Zucker (one year) for their involvement in the scheme.

Leonard was also fined $700,000. Leonard is due to make $50m in salary this season, while Ballmer, the former CEO of Microsoft, has an estimated wealth of $152.7bn, according to Forbes .

"The NBA's collectively bargained system for determining player compensation is a fundamental component of the basketball competition that the league oversees for the benefit of the teams and players and ultimately the fans," NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement. "I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers' institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations."

In a statement through his agent, Leonard said he took "full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family. I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap."

New York law firm Wachtell Lipton conducted the NBA's investigation into the matter after reporting by journalist Pablo Torre last year .

Torre, citing legal documents, claimed Ballmer employed Leonard for a non-existent role in one of his companies to circumvent the NBA salary cap, which punishes teams for spending too much on player salaries.

Torre claims that Ballmer partially funded a now defunct tree-planting company called Aspiration. That company then allegedly entered into a $28m agreement with KL2 Aspire, LLC, a company owned by Leonard.

Torre says he could find no evidence that Leonard had ever performed any work for Aspiration, and there was a clause in the contract between KL2 Aspire and Aspiration effectively allowed Leonard to be paid even if he did no work. Another clause said the deal would be voided if Leonard left the Clippers. One former employee of Aspiration told Torre he had heard the deal with Leonard had been set up to "circumvent the salary cap."

Wachtell Lipton's report concluded that the Clippers broke NBA rules after "initiating off-court income opportunities between Mr Leonard and four companies doing business with the team: Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance; facilitating endorsement agreements between these companies and Mr Leonard; inducing the companies to enter into these agreements by offering them business from the team; paying personal expenses on behalf of Mr Leonard and his representatives; and failing to report improper solicitations for off-court income opportunities made on Mr Leonard's behalf through his then-business manager, Dennis Robertson."

articles.title: Why Sonia Citron could be quietly important at the FIBA World Cup for Team USA
articles.summary: Need a bucket in the clutch? Call Sonia.
articles.body:
When the game is on the line, the Washington Mystics give the ball to Sonia Citron.

Kara Lawson and Team USA could do the same thing as they begin their pursuit of a fifth consecutive FIBA World Cup title on Friday.

The Americans might not have that many close games at the World Cup, which runs through Sept. 13 in Berlin, Germany. Team USA is the prohibitive favorite to win the tournament and win a record-extending 12th title.

But in clutch situations, Citron -- an injury replacement for Kelsey Plum -- is about as good as they come in the WNBA. That quality gives Team USA another leg up in a tight game, whether it comes in the group stage or in the final.

Citron is third in the WNBA in clutch shots attempted; these are shots defined as having an "elevated impact" on win probability. The two-time All-Star leads all players in what Inpredictable calls "clutch squared" shot attempts: shots that are crucial to a game's outcome, like a buzzer-beating 3-pointer.

Citron has hit six such "clutch squared" shots, all of which have been attempted in the final 2:01 of the fourth quarter or in overtime.

In all, 17.2 percent of Citron's shot attempts have been "clutch" shots, and 4.3 percent are "clutch squared." Both figures lead the WNBA.

Some players have the clutch gene. Others don't. Citron clearly does, and she is a huge reason why the Mystics have returned to the playoffs.

Postseason basketball could well follow a World Cup win in Germany later this month, when Citron could be a surprise contributor despite missing the initial 12-player Team USA roster.

articles.title: NBA suspends Clippers owner for a year, docks team first-round draft picks from Kawhi Leonard probe
articles.summary: In one of the largest basketball-related penalties ever levied against an NBA franchise in the league’s history, the NBA on Wednesday fined the Los Angeles Clippers $30 million and star Kawhi Leonard $700,000, suspended the team’s owner, Steve Ballmer, and two top executives and stripped the franchise of five first-round picks after ruling the team had circumvented the league’s salary cap rules.
articles.body: In one of the largest basketball-related penalties ever levied against an NBA franchise in the league’s history, the NBA on Wednesday fined the Los Angeles Clippers $30 million and star Kawhi Leonard $700,000, suspended the team’s owner, Steve Ballmer, and two top executives and stripped the franchise of five first-round picks after ruling the team had circumvented the league’s salary cap rules. Ballmer will be suspended from all league and team activities for one year for “knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities, for approving a business deal that he knew was a precondition for Aspiration to enter into an endorsement agreement with Mr. Leonard, and for his failure to create conditions under which his organization abided by the NBA’s circumvention rules,” the NBA ruled. NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement that he was “deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers’ institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct.” “The NBA’s collectively bargained system for determining player compensation is a fundamental component of the basketball competition that the league oversees for the benefit of the teams and players and ultimately the fans,” Silver added. Last year, the podcast “Pablo Torre Finds Out” reported Leonard had an endorsement deal with a former fintech company, Aspiration, worth millions that had never been publicly disclosed. The NBA enlisted the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen and Katz to perform an independent investigation that ultimately conducted 73 interviews of 60 people, according to a summary the league published Wednesday. According to the investigation, the Clippers broke league rules by initiating off-court income opportunities and facilitating endorsement agreements between Leonard and four companies that also did business with the team: Aspiration, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics and Lockton Insurance. The Clippers were “inducing the companies to enter into these agreements by offering them business from the team,” the league said. The Clippers also paid personal expenses for Leonard and his representatives and did not report “improper solicitations for off-court income opportunities” that Leonard’s uncle, Dennis Robertson, made on Leonard’s behalf. Leonard also violated league rules by “pressuring the Clippers to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses,” according to the league. Leonard must repay the NBA $700,000, and his uncle is banned from engaging with or conducting any business with NBA teams for five years. The Clippers had agreed to trade Leonard to the Toronto Raptors in July. “Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am,” Leonard said in a statement provided by his agent. “I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family.” Ballmer purchased the Clippers in 2014 after the NBA forced then-owner Donald Sterling to buy the team shortly after voice recordings of Sterling making racist statements became public. Under Ballmer, the tech titan who had earned billions as the former chief executive of Microsoft, the franchise was remade from one with an undesirable reputation into a destination because of Ballmer’s willingness to spend on staff and players, using his status as the wealthiest owner of a North American sports franchise. Ballmer poured billions into the team, including paying for its new Inglewood, California, arena that opened in 2024 and was used as the site of the NBA’s All-Star game last February. One of the team’s biggest coups was the signing of Leonard, the reigning MVP of the NBA Finals, as a free agent in 2019, while also trading for another star player, Paul George. The move instantly turned the Clippers, who have never made the NBA Finals, into a championship contender. But the team has only won three playoff series since and was not considered a championship contender entering the upcoming season that begins in October. The team will begin that season without its top basketball executive, Lawrence Frank, whom the NBA suspended for six months without pay as part of its investigation. Frank was involved “with the impermissible endorsement arrangements and for approving impermissible expenses incurred by Mr. Leonard and his family.” The team’s top business executive, Gillian Zucker, will be suspended without pay for one year, meanwhile, “for being primarily and directly culpable for the impermissible endorsement arrangements and for providing false and misleading statements to investigators.” Wachtell, Lipton Rosen and Katz wrote in its summary that its investigation was “challenged by, among other things, the approach of the Clippers and their outside counsel, who at times delayed in responding to requests for information and operated in an adversarial or obfuscatory manner that slowed investigators’ ability to gather the facts.” The team’s compliance with the penalties will be monitored by the league for the next five years.

articles.title: NBA: Los Angeles clippers fined $30m over Kawhi Leonard scandal
articles.summary: The LA Clippers are fined $30m (£22.2m) by the NBA for violating salary rules over the acquisition of star player Kawhi Leonard.
articles.body:
The LA Clippers have been fined $30m (£22.2m) by the National Basketball Association (NBA) for violating salary rules in order to funnel millions of dollars to star player Kawhi Leonard.

The fine - the largest in the league's history - comes after the NBA report said Leonard pressured the Clippers into "obtaining off-court income opportunities [and] successfully obtaining those opportunities".

The Clippers will also have to forfeit five first-round draft picks between 2029 and 2033, while owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended from all league and team activities for 12 months for his role in matters involving Leonard's sponsorship contracts during his time with the franchise.

The NBA said the Clippers had been guilty of "knowingly seeking to help Mr Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities".

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said he was "deeply disappointed" by the Clippers' "flagrant violations" of the rules and said he believed the "severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations".

Two-time NBA champion Leonard has been fined $700,000 (£518,997) by the league.

The team's president of business operations, Gillian Zucker, has been suspended for one year without pay for providing "misleading statements to investigators".

The punishments come after the NBA said its month-long investigation "found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organisation, a prior offender of the salary-cap circumvention rules".

Following the ruling, Leonard, 35, said he "accepts full responsibility" for his actions and "regrets the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family".

"I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap," he wrote on Instagram.

The two-time NBA Finals MVP joined the Clippers in 2019 and spent seven years with the franchise before leaving earlier this year.

The NBA said both the "organisation and personnel" of the Clippers will be subject to a compliance and monitoring programme overseen by the league for five years.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard punishment, investigation timeline: Why NBA disciplined Clippers, Steve Ballmer over salary-cap violations
articles.summary: The NBA initially launched its investigation into Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers in September 2025.
articles.body:
In an NBA offseason dominated by LeBron James and unrelated Lakers drama , Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers received a surprising amount of attention. And it all culminated with the NBA's announcement on Wednesday that its investigation into salary cap circumvention was complete .

The league stripped the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round draft picks and fined owner Steve Ballmer $30 million, with Leonard getting fined $700,000. Ballmer is suspended from all league and team activities for a year, while other Clippers executives were also punished.

So how did we get here, nearly a year since the NBA launched its investigation?

Below is a full timeline of the events leading up to the NBA's punishment, investigation and every significant development since Leonard's original agreement with the Clippers.

July 6, 2019: Kawhi Leonard signs with the Clippers

Fresh off a championship run with the Raptors, Leonard — a free agent — decided to leave Toronto to sign with the Clippers. He originally joined the team on a three-year, $103 million deal . That same offseason, the Clippers traded for Paul George. That influx of talent was supposed to make the Clippers a premier contender in the Western Conference.

Dec. 23, 2019: Reports suggest NBA investigated Clippers over Leonard signing

A few months after Leonard signed, a report from The Athletic detailed the superstar's free agency, which resulted in an NBA investigation. According to that report, one member of Leonard's camp — Dennis Robertson — reportedly asked teams for impermissible benefits if they wanted to sign Leonard. Robertson is also known as "Uncle Dennis," and is Leonard's actual uncle.

This was the key portion of The Athletic's report:

Sources say the league was told that Robertson asked team officials for part ownership of the team, a private plane that would be available at all times, a house and — last but certainly not least — a guaranteed amount of off-court endorsement money that they could expect if Leonard played for their team. All of those items, to be clear, would fall well outside the confines of the league's collective bargaining agreement.

It was believed Robertson made those requests to both the Raptors and the Los Angeles Lakers.

The NBA looked into whether the Clippers granted any of those requests, but an investigation found no evidence that was the case.

Months earlier, the NBA revamped its tampering and free-agent rules , perhaps as a response to the rumors surrounding Leonard's free agency.

Sept. 3, 2025: Pablo Torre prompts NBA to open another investigation into Clippers

Between December 2019 and August 2025, things are mostly quiet on the Leonard front. While he remained an elite player on the court, Leonard missed time here and there with injuries with the Clippers. Despite his original contract running out, Leonard continued to re-sign with the club, eventually landing on a deal that kept him under contract through the 2026-27 NBA season.

The Leonard-George pairing didn't work out as well as intended, with the Clippers failing to win a title with the two stars. George eventually left for the Philadelphia 76ers, and Leonard was set to open the 2025-26 NBA season with hopes of keeping the Clippers in contention in a tough Western Conference.

But a little over a month before the 2025-26 NBA season, journalist Pablo Torre released an episode of his podcast "Pablo Torre Finds Out" that accused the Clippers of using a sponsor to pay Leonard for "no-show jobs" as a way to circumvent the NBA salary cap.

That company — named Aspiration — was funded by Ballmer. During the show, Torre argued that Aspiration paid Leonard $28 million to essentially do nothing. Leonard would only be paid if he remained a member of the Clippers, per Torre. If Ballmer was aware of that arrangement, or encouraged it, that could constitute the Clippers circumventing the NBA salary cap, a significant violation. One former employee of Aspiration, which has since gone bankrupt, said they were told the agreement with Leonard was a way for the team to "circumvent the salary cap."

That same day, the Clippers released a statement denying all accusations made by Torre. The team said it was not unusual for team sponsors to reach agreements with players and that Ballmer and the team had no oversight of Leonard's agreement with Aspiration.

Given all the evidence revealed in Torre's program, the NBA announced it would launch an investigation into the situation.

Sept. 5, 2025: Steve Ballmer says he was conned by Aspiration

In his first interview since Torre's podcast, Ballmer claimed he was the victim of fraud by Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg.

"These are guys who committed fraud. Look, they conned me. I made an investment in these guys thinking it was on the up and up. And they conned me. At this stage, I have no ability to predict why they might have done anything they did."

Ballmer also reiterated that the Clippers introduced Leonard to Aspiration, which is not against NBA rules. From that point, Ballmer said the team was not involved in Leonard's negotiations with the company.

Sept. 10, 2025: Adam Silver addresses NBA investigation into Clippers, Leonard

Following a Board of Governors meeting in September, NBA commissioner Adam Silver publicly addressed the Leonard investigation for the first time. He didn't get into specifics, merely saying the NBA would need clear evidence suggesting the Clippers tried to circumvent the NBA salary cap.

Silver said the " mere appearance of impropriety " would not be enough to force the league to act.

Sept. 11, 2025: Torre unearths more evidence suggesting Clippers funded payments to Leonard

Torre, meanwhile, kept releasing episodes providing more suspicious evidence suggesting the Clippers may have known about and funded Leonard's deal with Aspiration.

Torre's next episode into the matter focused on Clippers co-owner Dennis Wong, who reportedly invested a hefty amount of money into the failing business just days before Leonard was set to be paid. It provided more evidence suggesting the Clippers were aware of the agreement between Leonard and Aspiration.

Sept. 16, 2025: Ballmer says he's confident he'll be cleared in NBA investigation

During an appearance at Sports Business Journal's Drive event, Ballmer said he welcomed the NBA investigation and remained steadfast that the team did not violate any rules when signing Leonard.

Sept. 18, 2025: Ballmer reportedly sent payments to Aspiration around time Leonard was due to be paid

Torre put out yet another episode of his program , this one focusing on payments Ballmer made to Aspiration just before Leonard was set to be paid. Torre found multiple instances in which the team or a member of the team made significant payments to Aspiration just days before Aspiration sent a large payment to Leonard.

There was still no smoking gun directly confirming Ballmer paid Leonard extra money through Aspiration, but enough evidence had been uncovered by Torre that the NBA couldn't look away.

Sept. 19, 2025-May 3, 2026: NBA goes silent, Torre keeps posting

After acknowledging a new investigation was launched, the NBA mostly went silent on all things involving the Clippers and Leonard. Torre, meanwhile, continued to post episodes with more evidence casting suspicion on the team and its actions. Torre posted one more video in September, and then a seven-and-a-half-hour compilation of every single episode on the topic in December.

In January, Torre started posting new videos on the Leonard situation. He posted a new video roughly every month between January and June, providing more evidence and going in depth on questionable agreements involving Leonard, Ballmer, the Clippers and the team's sponsors.

May 4, 2026: Torre wins Pulitzer Prize for unearthing Leonard situation

Torre received one of journalism's highest honors in May, when it was announced his show won a Pulitzer Prize for audio reporting . Torre won the award thanks to the program's deep dive into the Leonard situation.

June 1, 2026: Aspiration co-founder sentenced to 14 months in prison

Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg was sentenced to 14 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to two charges of wire fraud.

Two months earlier, Ballmer had his attorneys send a letter to the judge presiding over Sanberg's case. That letter outlined all the ways in which Ballmer believed he was defrauded by Sanberg and Aspiration.

June 30, 2026: Clippers trade Leonard to the Raptors

With the investigation still ongoing, the Clippers decided to trade Leonard to the Raptors. From a basketball perspective, the move made sense. The Clippers failed to make the playoffs despite Leonard posting excellent numbers last season. With the 35-year-old entering the final year of his contract, the Clippers had legitimate reasons for trading away the aging star.

The optics, however, were questionable at best. And given the investigation was still underway, it was unclear whether the NBA would be forced to address the issue now that Leonard was involved in a significant offseason transaction.

July 9, 2026: Clippers, Raptors say Leonard deal on hold for now

The NBA did address the trade, though not publicly. Both the Clippers and Raptors confirmed the Leonard deal was on hold until the NBA completed its investigation into the matter.

The Clippers used the opportunity to again reiterate that they did not funnel money to Leonard through Aspiration. The team added that it expects the trade to eventually be completed.

"On June 30, we reached an agreement in principle to trade Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors," the team said. "We have since been informed that the trade can only be finalized if the Raptors' ownership group assumes the risk of penalties related to Kawhi's contract that could theoretically result from the ongoing investigation. The investigation is ongoing, and we expect the trade to be finalized following its conclusion."

The Raptors said they were told they "would assume the risk of any potential outcome of the investigation impacting Kawhi" if they allowed the trade to go through now. With that uncertainty lingering, the team said it would wait until the league's investigation was complete before moving forward with the deal.

July 15, 2026: Silver publicly addresses Leonard trade, investigation

At the Summer League, Silver addressed both the Leonard trade and the status of the league's investigation . Silver said the league did not pause the Leonard deal, instead saying both the Clippers and Raptors made that decision.

Regarding the actual investigation, Silver said he hoped to have things resolved over the summer, before the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season.

That same day, it was reported that the NBA was looking into a separate endorsement deal Leonard had with a different company.

July 29, 2026: Reports emerge suggesting Leonard investigation could continue into 2027

While Silver said he hoped the NBA's investigation would cease before the start of the 2026-27 NBA season, reports emerged suggesting it could extend into 2027 .

An ESPN report claimed the issue could get pushed to next year, depending on whether all parties agreed with the findings of law firm Wachtell Lipton, which the NBA hired to perform its investigation. That report seemed to suggest the league's investigation was over … or at least close to being concluded.

Aug. 7, 2026: Torre reports on another questionable Leonard deal

Torre dropped another bombshell in August, reporting on a deal Leonard signed with the company Daktronics. Despite seemingly not doing any endorsement work for the company, Leonard reportedly received millions from Daktronics.

Torre claimed that some people who worked on the Intuit Dome were "openly" joking about the deal as being "1,000% a way to circumvent the salary cap."

Aug. 17, 2026: ESPN reports NBA has no evidence Ballmer funneled money to Leonard

The NBA's investigation into Leonard, the Clippers and Ballmer reportedly found no evidence Ballmer funneled money to Leonard , ESPN reported.

Despite that, the NBA was still looking into other potential violations by the team, with ESPN reporting "both sides have been negotiating a resolution to the investigation."

Shortly after that report emerged, the NBA said there were inaccuracies in ESPN's reporting. ESPN stood by its article.

In response to that piece, the Clippers once again released a statement claiming they did not funnel money to Leonard. The team also reiterated that introducing players to sponsors is not against NBA rules.

ESPN also reported that any punishment from the league would likely be taken to arbitration by Ballmer and/or the NBPA, which wouldn't look kindly on a player being punished for working with a team sponsor.

Sept. 2, 2026, Part I: Feds, NBA investigating Daktronics

The Securities and Exchange Commission opened an investigation into scoreboard manufacturer Daktronics on Wednesday in relation to an alleged sponsorship deal the company had with Los Angeles Clippers star Kawhi Leonard .

Daktronics acting CFO Howard Atkins revealed the investigation on an earnings call Wednesday, and said they have received requests for information from the NBA. Specifics of the SEC's investigation are not yet known. It marked the first public acknowledgment that the NBA is including Daktronics in its investigation into Leonard and the Clippers.

"As you might expect, we have received requests for information from the NBA. Additionally, the Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from us concerning the company and Mr. Leonard," Atkins said . "We take these requests seriously and are cooperating. At this point, out of respect for the respective processes, we will not be providing further comment."

Sept. 2, 2026, Part II: NBA announces conclusion of investigation, punishment

Shortly after, the NBA announced that its nearly year-long investigation concluded , and stripped the Clippers of five first-round draft picks, fined Ballmer $30 million and Leonard $700,000.

Ballmer is suspended from all league and team activities for one year, while Clippers president of business operations Gillian Zucker was suspended without pay for one year, and president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank was suspended six months without pay. The league also banned Dennis Robertson from conducting business or engaging with NBA teams for five years.

The Clippers will lose their first-round picks in the 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033 NBA Drafts.

Leonard, who has since been traded to the Toronto Raptors in a deal that's been held up by the NBA's investigation, released a statement on social media shortly after the league's announcement.

The Clippers released a statement saying they "vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence.

"What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure it's fairness and accuracy."

The team said it would challenge the league's punishment.

Oct. 20, 2026: Opening night of the 2026-27 NBA season

The 2026-27 NBA regular season is set to begin Oct. 20. Three games will occur that day , none of which will feature either the Clippers or Raptors. Those teams will play their first games the following day, Oct. 21.

articles.title: NBA levies astonishing penalty against Clippers over cap circumvention involving Steve Ballmer, Kawhi Leonard
articles.summary: Steve Ballmer faces a $30 million fine and one-year suspension as the NBA strips five first-round picks from the Los Angeles Clippers over cap violations.
articles.body: The NBA stripped five first-round draft picks from the Los Angeles Clippers, fined owner Steve Ballmer $30 million and suspended key executives after a yearlong investigation found that the team circumvented salary-cap rules in connection with Kawhi Leonard. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, the Clippers will forfeit their first-round picks from 2029 through 2033, which absolutely guts their draft capital for the next decade. It’s a punishment so severe that the NBA has rarely, if ever, dropped the hammer this hard. The NBA cited "a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations," determining that team officials systematically coordinated off-the-books arrangements rather than making an isolated error. BIG PICTURE DETAILS The closest precedent came in 2000, when the NBA voided Minnesota’s contracts with Joe Smith, stripped the Timberwolves of five first-round picks and fined the team $3.5 million over a secret agreement involving the forward. The Clippers now face an even broader punishment, including multiple executive suspensions and five years of league monitoring. Ballmer is suspended for one year from all league and team activities. Investigators determined that the billionaire owner knowingly helped Leonard pursue off-court income opportunities, approved an arrangement tied to Leonard’s Aspiration endorsement deal and failed to ensure the Clippers complied with salary-cap rules. NFL FINES SAINTS AND COWBOYS $500K FOR PRACTICE BRAWL, BUT FIGHTS WON'T STOP UNLESS PLAYERS GET FINED President of Business Operations Gillian Zucker received a one-year unpaid suspension after investigators deemed her primarily responsible for the improper deals and accused her of providing false and misleading statements during the probe. President of Basketball Operations Lawrence Frank received a six-month unpaid suspension for his involvement in the arrangements and for approving improper expenses incurred by Leonard and his family. GIANNIS ANTETOKOUNMPO ERA TO END IN MILWAUKEE AS BUCKS WILL SEND TWO-TIME MVP TO MIAMI HEAT FOR YOUNG CORE Leonard avoided a game suspension and a voided contract but must pay $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits funneled to his former representative, Dennis Robertson. Robertson was permanently barred from conducting business with the NBA. Leonard cut ties with him in June. In a statement issued through agent Harrison Gaines, Leonard denied wrongdoing while accepting responsibility for "lapses in judgment" by his inner circle. "Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am," Leonard said. "I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family." "I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone’s part to circumvent the salary cap. "For 15 years, my priority has been giving everything to my family, the game and those I share the court with. As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter and moving forward with a clean slate." The Clippers mortgaged their entire future for a single championship window, and now they’ll spend the next decade paying off the debt. articles.title: Pablo Torre, Mark Cuban, others react after NBA punishes the Clippers and Kawhi Leonard in sponsorship scandal
articles.summary: Mark Cuban had previously sparred with Pablo Torre, both on his podcast and on social media, over the Kawhi Leonard-Clippers investigation.
articles.body:
The NBA came down on Kawhi Leonard and the Los Angeles Clippers hard on Wednesday afternoon.

The league announced that it had stripped the Clippers of five first-round draft picks and fined Clippers owner Steve Ballmer , among other things, after it had determined that the team circumvented the salary cap rules.

Journalist Pablo Torre, who first unveiled the possible violations on his "Pablo Torre Finds Out" podcast and has been covering developments of the scandal every step of the way, was quick to take to social media after the ruling was announced. He responded with just a single emoji.

Torre has alleged that there were at least two lucrative no-show sponsorship deals that companies struck with Leonard. The first was involving the now-defunct sustainability company Aspiration , which reportedly paid Leonard millions for no visible work. The second allegedly involved scoreboard company Daktronics, which is a business-to-business company with no history of celebrity sponsorship deals. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Daktronics now, too.

All of this, Torre alleged, was done in an effort to circumvent the NBA's salary-cap rules after he signed with the team in 2019.

The NBA handed down several punishments on Wednesday. The league stripped the Clippers of five future first-round draft picks, one in every draft from 2029 to 2033. Ballmer was fined $30 million and suspended. Clippers president Lawrence Frank and president of business operations Gillian Zucker were suspended, too. Leonard was also hit with a $700,000 fine.

The Clippers said in a statement that they "vehemently reject the NBA's findings," and called the investigation "heavily biased."

It was the scope of the punishment that left many stunned, and sent people rushing to compare it to what other leagues have done.

There were also plenty of jokes to be made, especially since Leonard was told he had to pay $700,000. The deal to send him to the Toronto Raptors will now seemingly be allowed to go through.

Perhaps the best reaction was from former Dallas Mavericks majority owner Mark Cuban, who had sparred with Torre on both social media and on his podcast over the issue and repeatedly defended Ballmer .

Torre's reporting, for which he won a Pulitzer Prize, ended up being accurate. Cuban's sentiment was one many shared.

articles.title: Clippers Will Appeal NBA Punishment, 'Vehemently Reject' Findings from Kawhi Leonard Investigation
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers plan to appeal the NBA's significant list of punishments the league announced Wednesday following an investigation into the franchise and Kawhi Leonard.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers plan to appeal the NBA's significant list of punishments the league announced Wednesday following an investigation into the franchise and Kawhi Leonard.

The Clippers released a statement that said they "vehemently reject" the league's decision:

"We vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence. What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure its fairness and accuracy.

"For the past year, we cooperated fully and in good faith and we will now fight just as hard to demonstrate our innocence.

"We intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process."

The team also sent NBA commissioner Adam Silver a lengthy letter:

It should be noted the NBA does not have a formal appeal or arbitration process the franchise can use for this situation:

According to the NBA's statement, the Clippers engaged in "a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations" that included "violating the salary cap circumvention rules contained in the league's Collective Bargaining Agreement."

It also said Leonard and his then-business manager, Dennis Robertson, "violated the circumvention rules by pressuring the Clippers to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses."

Here is the full list of CBA rules the NBA said the Clippers broke:

"The NBA's collectively bargained system for determining player compensation is a fundamental component of the basketball competition that the league oversees for the benefit of the teams and players and ultimately the fans," Silver said in the announcement. "I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers' institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations."

Those penalties included a $30 million fine for the Clippers, the forfeiture of five first-round draft picks (one each in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033), a $700,000 fine for Leonard, a one-year suspension from all league and team activities for Clippers governor Steve Ballmer, and a sixth-month suspension without pay for Clippers president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank.

Leonard also issued a statement through his agent, Harrison Gaines, that said, in part, "I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family."

Los Angeles agreed to trade the seven-time All-Star to the Toronto Raptors this offseason, although that move was paused during the investigation.

articles.title: Clippers docked 5 first-round draft picks and fined $30 million following Kawhi Leonard probe
articles.summary: The NBA penalizes the LA Clippers with a $30M fine and forfeits five first-round draft picks following an investigation into Kawhi Leonard’s cap circumvention.
articles.body: The NBA issued stern penalties against the Los Angeles Clippers on Wednesday following an independent investigation that revealed a “pattern of misconduct” and severe salary cap circumvention violations. The investigation found that the Clippers improperly funneled off-court endorsement opportunities to star forward Kawhi Leonard through corporate partners – including Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance – in exchange for team business. The report stated the franchise also covered personal expenses for Leonard and failed to report improper solicitations made by his former business manager, Dennis Robertson. As a result of this investigation, the Clippers must forfeit five consecutive first-round draft picks starting in 2029, pay a $30 million fine and submit to five years of strict league monitoring. Clippers owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended for one year from all league and team activities for, in part, “failure to create conditions under which his organization abided by the NBA’s circumvention rules.” In a sharp rebuttal, the Clippers organization vehemently rejected the league’s findings, calling the probe a “heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence.” The team claimed that public announcements contradicted private assurances from league officials and maintained that introducing players to corporate partners aligns with standard NBA practices. Ballmer’s attorney David Kelley escalated the feud in a letter the Clippers said it sent to NBA Commissioner Adam Silver, which the team posted on X. The letter criticized the investigation as “flawed from the outset” and called the process a “witch hunt” designed to enforce a predetermined outcome. The team accused the league of contradicting private admissions—including previous assurances that Ballmer was a victim of fraud rather than a conspirator—and warned it is “exploring every legal remedy to address this gross injustice.” CNN has reached out to the NBA on the letter. Leonard, a two-time NBA champion, is required to pay $700,000 in restitution to the NBA. Through his agent Harrison Gaines, the two-time Finals MVP issued a statement denying he knew about “anyone’s part to circumvent the salary cap” while addressing the findings. “Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am. I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused,” he stated. The seven-time All-Star said he was looking ahead to his second stint with his former team, the Raptors, next season. “As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate,” he added. Silver condemned the “flagrant violations” and “the Clippers’ institutional and leadership failures,” noting the severity of the punishment reflects the seriousness of the offense. Despite the Clippers’ vow to challenge the ruling, the effort appears to be moot, with both the NBA and the players’ union confirming the penalties are final and cannot be appealed by any party. CNN has reached out to Ballmer for comment. The Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz law firm conducted the probe. Penalties announced nearly a year after report The NBA’s findings land almost a year to the date after the league said it would investigate the team following a report by podcast host and journalist Pablo Torre. He accused the Clippers of orchestrating a deceptive endorsement deal to sign the then-free agent Leonard through noncompliant ways. In an episode of “Pablo Torre Finds Out” released in September 2025, Torre claimed to have gained access to more than 3,000 pages of internal documents and spoke with multiple unnamed sources. Those documents and sources, Torre reports, put together a picture of an alleged 2022 scheme to pay Leonard $28 million over four years, which would avoid the league’s salary restrictions. Following the start of the probe, Leonard, Ballmer and the team denied any wrongdoing. Ballmer and team president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank also said they “welcomed the league’s investigation” at the time. Frank was suspended on Wednesday without pay for six months along with team president of business operations Gillan Zucker, who was suspended for a year. According to the report, Ballmer invested $50 million in Aspiration before the team and company announced a $300 million partnership in September 2021, just about a month after Leonard signed a four-year, $176 million extension with the Clippers. The Clippers terminated the relationship two years later, citing contract default. Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg agreed to plead guilty in August 2025 after facing federal wire fraud charges. Prosecutors said he defrauded investors and lenders out of $248 million, adding that “Aspiration’s financial statements were inaccurate and reflected much higher revenue than the company in fact received.” When Aspiration filed for bankruptcy, the company still owed Leonard roughly $7 million of his $28 million endorsement deal, according to Torre’s report. Leonard previously downplayed the unpaid funds, calling the arrangement a “fraud” and claiming he never received the money. This story has been updated with additional reporting.

articles.title: La mejor jugadora china no jugará el Mundial por perder su pasaporte
articles.standfirst: Se trata de Li Yueru (2,01, 27 años), la líder del equipo asiático en los pasados Juegos
articles.summary: Se trata de Li Yueru (2,01, 27 años), la líder del equipo asiático en los pasados Juegos
articles.body: A dos días de comenzar el Mundial de baloncesto, la selección de China sufre un varapalo casi decisivo. No podrá contar con su mejor jugadora, Li Yueru (2,01 y 27 años), por la estrambótica razón de que su pasaporte se perdió en el correo. Eso al menos es lo que ha dicho la jugadora de las Dallas Wings en las redes sociales, donde anunció que no jugará el Mundial. Es una baja decisiva para China porque se trata de una de las piezas que más sentido da al juego de las asiáticas. De hecho en los pasados Juegos Olímpicos Yueru promedió 17,7 puntos, 11 rebotes y 21,7 de valoración. Esta temporada en Dallas estaba limitada a 3,3 puntos y 2,6 rebotes, pero ha demostrado que es una jugadora muy dominante en el baloncesto FIBA femenino. China está encuadrada en el grupo D junto a Estados Unidos, la República Checa e Italia. Este es el mensaje completo de Li Yueru en las redes: "Gracias a todos los que se han acordado de mí y se han interesado por cómo estoy", escribe la jugadora. "En los últimos años, he mantenido una excelente relación con la Asociación China de Baloncesto y con la selección nacional. Siempre han sido un gran apoyo a lo largo de mi carrera en el extranjero. La selección siempre me ha hecho sentir valorada y apreciada, y ha sido un inmenso honor representar a China. Estaba increíblemente ilusionada y entusiasmada ante la idea de volver a unirme a la selección nacional. Por desgracia, mi pasaporte se extravió en el correo y aún no ha aparecido. Durante todo este tiempo, hemos trabajado juntos y explorado todas las soluciones posibles, pero quizá esta vez nos haya faltado un poco de suerte. A día de hoy, el pasaporte sigue sin aparecer. A veces, la decepción forma parte de la vida. Me entristece no poder estar presente en esta ocasión, pero estoy increíblemente agradecida a todos los que me han apoyado y a quienes siguen apoyando el baloncesto femenino chino. Gracias por todo vuestro amor y apoyo. ¡Nos vemos pronto en la escena mundial!"
